name: obesity-fastfood-paired-annual

recipe.subtitle: Obesity: share of adults, from a CDC telephone survey.

dataset.label: Obesity and fast food by state (CDC + Census, annual)
dataset.source: CDC (BRFSS) and U.S. Census Bureau (County Business Patterns)
dataset.source_line: Sources: CDC BRFSS (obesity); U.S. Census Bureau, County Business Patterns (restaurants)
dataset.license: Both are U.S. Government works in the public domain. CDC asks that BRFSS be cited and notes its values are self-reported survey estimates; the Census Bureau asks that CBP be cited and withholds small cells for disclosure avoidance.

sources.name: CDC, Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS)
sources.license: U.S. Government work, public domain (17 USC 105). CDC asks that BRFSS be cited and notes the values are self-reported survey estimates.

sources.name: U.S. Census Bureau, County Business Patterns (CBP)
sources.license: U.S. Government work, public domain (17 USC 105). The Census Bureau asks that CBP be cited; small cells are withheld for disclosure avoidance.

dataset.notes: Obesity from the CDC DNPAO BRFSS extract (question: percent of adults 18+ with obesity, Total stratification). Restaurants from CBP NAICS 722513, queried at state level so disclosure suppression -- which removes hundreds of counties a year with no flag -- does not silently undercount. 722211 became 722513 in 2012 and is bridged as a code change, not a break.

methodology_breaks.what: BRFSS added cell-phone households and changed its weighting; CDC states that estimates from 2011 forward cannot be compared with earlier ones.
methodology_breaks.effect: The window starts here. Extending it earlier is refused rather than spliced.

methodology_breaks.what: County Business Patterns moved from SIC to NAICS. SIC 5812 'Eating Places' covers full-service and fast food together; the limited-service class (722513) does not exist before NAICS.
methodology_breaks.effect: Not a renumbering and not bridgeable. The pre-1998 SIC era is a different measure, and it predates every CDC series here in any case.

derivations.method: this year's establishment count minus 2011's, floored at zero
derivations.numerator: Census CBP, NAICS 722513 establishment counts at state level
derivations.denominator: none: a difference, not a rate
derivations.assumption: none: a difference of two published counts. It is a NET change -- openings minus closures -- because CBP publishes a level and not events.

derivations.method: establishment count divided by resident population, times 100,000
derivations.numerator: Census CBP, NAICS 722513 establishment counts at state level
derivations.denominator: Census Population Estimates Program resident population, county rows summed to states, the later vintage winning a whole shared YEAR (not each county: Connecticut's eras use different FIPS and a per-county rule summed both sets)
derivations.assumption: none: quotient of two published counts
